title: Send coding tasks from a chat bot to your coding agents
summary: A developer says he routes coding tasks from a Grok bot to Claude Code and Codex through Conductor, saving thousands of Grok credits over several weeks.
agent_role: A chat bot receives coding requests and hands them to Claude Code and Codex running in Conductor's cloud. The human set up the connection and delegates the tasks.
outcome: Author reports it saved him thousands of credits on Grok.
what_they_did: The poster got a Conductor cloud plan and turned off Grok's built-in coding feature in settings. He made a bot connected to Conductor through a connector. He now sends all coding tasks to that bot, which runs them on his own Claude Code and Codex subscriptions.
how_it_went: He says he has used it for weeks and it saved him thousands of credits on Grok.
worth_knowing: It relies on paid plans for Conductor, Claude Code and Codex, so the savings depend on what you already pay for.
prompt: Set up a workflow where coding requests I send you are passed to my coding agents at [coding service] instead of being done here. Connect to [coding service] using my account, then for each request: write a clear task, send it to the right agent, and report back with a summary of changes. Show me each task before sending it, and never merge or deploy without my approval.

curation.rationale: A concrete, step-by-step setup for handing coding work from a chat bot to existing coding agent subscriptions. It is thin, with only a vague savings claim.
